newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's Chart Thai Party said to have refused to endorse a plan by the other coalition partners to nominate Defence Minister, Gen Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, as his successor. The party has decided to give Banharn the ultimate power to negotiate with coalition partners on the selection of a new prime minister. (THE NATION)

- PM Banharn has told members of his Chart Thai Party that he felt he had been cheated by his coalition partners, especially New Aspiration leader Chavalit. He says the scheme to destroy him politically and oust him from the premiership had been engineered by New Aspiration, Nam Thai and Muan Chon parties. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Cabinet has allowed the Metropolitan Rapid Transit Authority to award a $23.9 billion baht subway construction contract Ch Karnchang Plc's BCKT unit. The agency says the contract could be signed within two months. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Bank of Thailand will control lending through Bangkok International Banking Facilities from the end of this month. Out-in lending will be fixed as a percentage of out-out lending in a bid to reduce Thailand's exposure to risk from short-term debt. (BANGKOK POST)

- Government officials have completed the drafting of a new "white paper" on economic relations with Japan, marking a shift from the donor-recipient status towards a partnership in which both countries will play a cooperative role in development of Indochina and nearby areas. (THE NATION)
- Daimler-Benz AG plans to set up a leasing company in a joint venture with Viriyah Leasing Co Ltd early next year in a move to play a bigger role in Thailand's automobile industry. (THE NATION)

- Thai hotel operator, the Dusit Thani Group, says it may be forced to close its flagship property in downtown Bangkok due to disruption caused by construction of a subway station beneath the hotel's car park. (BUSINESS DAY)
